Sometimes I’ll be alone and I’ll hear the TV from next door or people outside, and then it makes me think about what they’re saying or what they’re planning, because people do talk, you know? Like my aunt used to whisper in the kitchen and then say she wasn’t saying anything. But voices, like just out of nowhere? I haven’t really noticed that.\n\nDoctor: Do people ever tell you that your speech is hard to follow or that your thoughts seem jumbled?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… people say I talk “too much” or I don’t get to the point, but that’s because there’s a lot of parts to it. Like if I’m explaining one thing, I have to explain what happened before, otherwise they’ll twist it and say I never said that. My sister does that, she’ll act like she doesn’t remember, and then suddenly everyone is looking at me like I’m the confusing one.\n\nSo… hard to follow? Maybe they say that, but I don’t think my thoughts are jumbled. I think they just don’t want to listen all the way.\n\nDoctor: Before this money issue started, did you generally have a hard time trusting people?\n\nPatient: I don’t know… I mean, what do you mean by “hard time”? I always noticed when people were acting funny, if that’s what you mean. But everybody notices stuff, right? Like if someone says they’ll call and then they don’t, or they smile one way in front of you and another way when someone else walks in.\n\nBefore all this, I guess I just kept my eyes open. My grandma used to say you don’t tell everybody your business, because people use it. And she wasn’t wrong—there was this lady at the corner store who would repeat everything she heard, even about people’s kids, and then act innocent. So trusting people… I don’t know. I trusted some people. Not everybody. You can’t trust everybody.\n\nDoctor: Before the money problem began, did you often think people were trying to take advantage of you?\n\nPatient: I don’t know if I’d say “often.” I mean, people try to get over on people all the time, that’s just how it is. Like at stores, they’ll ring something up wrong and then act like you’re bothering them when you ask. And my cousin used to borrow little things and not bring them back, but everybody acted like that was normal because she was “family.”\n\nBefore the money thing… I guess I noticed when somebody wasn’t being straight. But taking advantage, like everybody was out to do that? I don’t know. I wasn’t walking around thinking that all day. I just didn’t like being played, that’s all.\n\nDoctor: Do you think there is anything impossible or beyond ordinary methods about how they are hiding your money?\n\nPatient: I don’t mean like magic or something, if that’s what you’re asking. It’s ordinary ways, but sneaky ways. Like they keep showing me these bank papers and saying, “See, nothing was taken,” but papers can be moved around, bills can be made to look one way, and then there’s fundraisers and trip plans mixed in so nobody can tell what went where.\n\nThat’s why I keep asking them, because it’s been over a year and I know they’re hiding my money. They want me to stop bringing it up, but if I stop, then they just get away with it. My family and even friends keep acting like I’m not seeing it right, but they’re covering it up. They need to just tell the truth.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever felt like someone could put thoughts into your mind or take thoughts out of it?\n\nPatient: Put thoughts in? I don’t… I don’t think so. Like, people can get in your head by talking too much, you know? My aunt does that, she’ll keep saying the same thing until you start hearing it even when she’s not there, but that’s not like taking thoughts out.\n\nI’ve had people try to confuse me, definitely. They say things one way and then later say they never said it, and then you start questioning yourself. But someone actually putting a thought in my mind or removing one… I don’t know. I haven’t noticed that kind of thing.\n\nDoctor: Is it possible you could be mistaken about your family hiding your money?\n\nPatient: Mistaken? I mean… people keep saying that, that I’m “mistaken,” because they wave the bank papers around like that proves everything. But papers don’t show everything. Bills get moved around, fundraisers, trips, all that stuff gets mixed together, and then nobody can tell where the money really went.\n\nAnd my family keeps acting like I’m the problem for asking. My friends too, they say to leave it alone, but it’s been over a year. I know they’re hiding it. I didn’t come here because I’m confused about that, I came because everybody keeps trying to make me stop talking about it. If they would just tell the truth, I wouldn’t have to keep confronting them.\n\nDoctor: Aside from this issue with your money, have you been able to work and handle your usual day-to-day responsibilities normally?\n\nPatient: Yeah, I mean, mostly. I don’t have a job right now, but I still do my regular things. I make my own food, I get myself to the county clinic and those assistance appointments, and I keep my stuff in order.\n\nIt’s really just when the money thing comes up, then there’s arguing, because they act like I’m supposed to just forget it. But day to day, I’m not helpless or anything. I do what I have to do.\n\nDoctor: Have people told you that you seem emotionally flat or don’t show much feeling?\n\nPatient: Emotionally flat? I don’t know… people say all kinds of things when they want you to stop talking. My cousin will say I’m “cold” if I don’t react the way she wants, but then if I do get upset, she says I’m making a scene, so what am I supposed to do with that?\n\nI mean, I laugh at things. I get mad, I get worried. Maybe I don’t always show it on my face right away. Sometimes I’m just thinking, and people think that means something. I don’t know if that’s the same as flat. What do you mean by that exactly?\n\nDoctor: Have there been times when you felt unusually energetic or high, like you needed much less sleep than usual?\n\nPatient: Unusually energetic… I don’t know. I have nights where I don’t sleep good, but that’s not like I’m “high” or whatever. Sometimes I’m just thinking too much, and then the next day I’m tired and people still expect me to go stand in lines at those offices, and the buses don’t even run right half the time.\n\nSo… less sleep, maybe sometimes, but not because I’m feeling great or anything. I don’t think I get that way. What do you mean by unusually energetic?\n\nDoctor: Other than the money issue, do you believe anyone is trying to harm, cheat, or spy on you?\n\nPatient: I mean… not spy like cameras or anything, if that’s what you mean. But cheat, yeah, that’s kind of the whole thing. My family and some people I thought were friends keep acting like the bank papers prove nothing happened, but they don’t. They’re hiding where the money went.\n\nIt’s been over a year, and every time I bring it up there’s some new excuse—bills, or some fundraiser, or somebody planning a trip like that’s supposed to explain everything. And then they say I’m the problem because I keep asking. But if someone was taking from you and covering it up, you wouldn’t just sit there either. So I keep confronting them because somebody needs to finally tell the truth.\n\nDoctor: Before the money problem started, did you often believe people were deliberately plotting against you?\n\nPatient: Before? I mean, people have always had their little ways, you know, saying one thing and doing another, but this isn’t me just thinking everybody’s plotting.
